question: What are the places where the groundwater is stored between layers of hard rock below the water table called?
solution:
The correct answer is Aquifer.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**__Aquifer:__

 
• It is a saturated area beneath the water table.
 
• It is basically an underground layer of water-bearing permeable rock, rock fractures, or unconsolidated materials.
 
• They are huge storehouses of water.
 
• Aquifers are of two types:
 
 
• Confined Aquifer: It is an aquifer below the land surface that is saturated with water.
 
• Unconfined Aquifer: It is an aquifer where the groundwater is in direct contact with the atmosphere through the open pore spaces of the overlying soil or rock.
